definition: pandas gives Python labelled tables (DataFrames) for loading, cleaning, joining and summarising data.
details: Created by Wes McKinney at AQR Capital in 2008 and open-sourced in 2009; now a NumFOCUS-sponsored community project.

explainer.lead: How to install pandas, a first working example, and where it fits in an AI project.
explainer.createdBy: Created by Wes McKinney; community maintained under NumFOCUS.

quickstart.python:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.read_csv("reviews.csv")          # columns: text, stars
df = df.dropna()
df["positive"] = df["stars"] >= 4
print(df.groupby("positive")["text"].count())

explainer.inAi: Most training sets start life as a DataFrame: clean and label the rows, split train/test, then pass df.values to scikit-learn or turn it into a Hugging Face Dataset.
explainer.jsNote: No official JavaScript version; Danfo.js is a community library with a pandas-like API.
